S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is characterized by at least one lifetime manic episode, often accompanied by major depressive episodes, leading to marked impairment in functioning or need for hospitalization. Manic episodes involve a sustained period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy and associated changes in thinking, behavior, and impulse control, while depressive episodes feature low mood and loss of interest with cognitive and physical slowing. The course is typically recurrent and episodic, with periods of relative euthymia between episodes, though residual symptoms and functional difficulties may persist. It is distinguished from Bipolar II by the presence of full mania (rather than hypomania) and from unipolar depression by a history of such manic episodes, often emerging or becoming more apparent in the context of psychosocial stressors, sleep disruption, or major life transitions.

patient.stressor: Anthony’s mood symptoms intensified after he picked up extra double shifts at the restaurant to save for a long‑planned trip and to pay down credit card debt from dropping out of college. The combination of late nights, irregular meals, and constantly changing schedules culminated in a period where he suddenly felt he could handle everything at once: he began volunteering for every busy shift, pitching multiple new menu concepts to management, and staying up all night sketching business plans for a pop‑up food truck, all while insisting he didn’t need rest. Over the next few months, this overextension at work gave way to a prolonged downturn in which he called out of shifts, stopped playing soccer, and struggled to keep up even basic tasks like paying bills and grocery shopping, putting his job at risk and straining his reputation as a reliable mentor to new staff. When his manager pulled him aside about erratic performance and his mother expressed concern about dramatic changes in his energy and drive, he agreed—reluctantly at first—to see a mental health professional through the clinic his employer’s insurance covered.
patient.chief_complaint: “I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to live for playing Sunday soccer and trying out new recipes after work, but lately even the thought of lacing up my cleats or cooking anything more than microwave noodles just feels pointless, so I mostly sit around scrolling on my phone until I fall asleep.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: When I was on that high streak I’d go whole shifts without eating and barely notice, and now it’s flipped so I either forget to eat all day or suddenly inhale a whole pizza at midnight because I realize I’m starving, and my clothes are starting to hang off me.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: There are days when I’m moving so slowly at the restaurant that carrying a tray from the kitchen to a table feels like walking through mud, and other days when I can’t stop pacing between the bar and the back room, fidgeting and bouncing my leg like I’m about to jump out of my skin.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how long I sleep or lie in bed, I wake up feeling wiped out, like my body’s a dead weight, and even showering and getting dressed for a shift feels like I’ve already done a full day’s work.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: My head feels foggy all the time now—customers will tell me their order and by the time I punch it into the screen I’ve already forgotten half of it, and even simple stuff like deciding what to buy at the store can leave me just standing there staring at the shelves.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: It’s like a switch flips and I go from feeling on top of the world—cracking jokes, hugging coworkers, planning three businesses in my head—to snapping at people over tiny things, like a messed‑up ticket or someone bumping into me, and I can’t seem to dial it back.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: When I’m up, I can’t sit still for a second—I sign up for every double, reorganize the whole server station, deep‑clean my apartment at 3 a.m., and start new projects before I’m halfway done with the last one, as if I’ve got this endless engine running inside me.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: During that big upswing I was completely convinced I could turn the restaurant around, launch a food truck, and be running my own chain in a year, and I was talking to my manager like I already knew more about the business than he did even though I never finished school.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: On my high days I just talk and talk—about new menu ideas, my travel plans, random stories from work—jumping from one thing to another so fast that people can’t get a word in and I feel almost physically uncomfortable if there’s a pause in the conversation.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My brain can get so revved up that thoughts are flying through faster than I can grab them—one second I’m thinking about paying off my credit card, then I’m planning a trip to Europe, then I’m redesigning the restaurant logo in my head, all at once, and I can’t slow it down enough to focus on anything.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: For a while there I was volunteering for every shift, texting old friends to hang out after close, hitting the gym at weird hours, and staying up all night sketching out business plans and menus for this food truck idea, like I had to keep doing things every minute or I’d explode.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over these months I’ve gone from being one of the most reliable servers to getting written up for no‑shows and mistakes, I’ve fallen behind on rent and bills, and I’ve pretty much stopped seeing friends outside of work because I’m either too wired and overwhelming or too drained to leave my apartment.
add_requirements.duration: All of this back‑and‑forth between feeling unstoppable and then completely drained has been going on for about four months, starting when I began stacking all those extra double shifts to save money.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: This heavy, low stretch where I can barely get myself to work or do basic things around the apartment has been hanging over me for around three months now.
